summary: The evidence does not establish a cause for the duplicate orders. order-router began logging 'idempotency key not found for retried webhook, treating as new order' at 14:10:11Z, and duplicate_orders rose from 0 to 5.4 in the 14:10 bucket and stayed elevated (18.0 at 15:05). Two candidate triggers exist: the 14:02 order-router dependency bump (deploy 00601) and the 14:07 redis-cache maxmemory cut. Neither is confirmed, and each has significant weak spots. The leading possibilities are the redis-cache eviction (H1) and the order-router dependency bump (H2), and slow broker-gateway responses (H3) could at most be a retry trigger paired with one of them. It is also unverified whether two broker orders were actually executed, as opposed to being treated as new by order-router.

hypotheses.statement: The 14:07 redis-cache maxmemory cut (4gb to 1gb, allkeys-lru) caused mass eviction from 14:10, which dropped idempotency/dedupe keys so retried webhooks missed lookup and were treated as new orders. This is weak because the first eviction log trails the first duplicate warning, and order-router has no graph edge to redis-cache.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: The 14:07 redis-cache config change cut maxmemory from 4gb to 1gb with allkeys-lru, shortly before the duplicates began.
Evictions began at 14:10 (evicted_keys 0 to 6000, then 12000 by 14:11) and memory_pct climbed from 60% to 97% over 14:09-14:11, so mass eviction was under way within the incident window.

contradicting.text: The first eviction log is at 14:10:35Z, after the first duplicate-path warning at 14:10:11Z, so eviction is not shown to precede the first duplicate. The one-minute metric bucket cannot resolve this.

order-router has no graph edge to redis-cache (only postgres and broker-gateway), and its logs show no redis lines, so it is not shown to use redis for dedupe. It is likely, though unverified, that its idempotency keys live in postgres.
The config change at 14:07 produced no step in memory_pct and no evictions until 14:10.
Even if it were involved, it is only an assumption that dedupe keys were among the evicted keys; the logs name no keys.

hypotheses.statement: The 14:02 order-router dependency bump (deploy 00601) changed idempotency-key generation or the retry client, so retried webhooks no longer match stored keys and are treated as new orders, which gives duplicates from about 14:10.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: order-router deploy 00601 (a 'dependency bump') went out at 14:02, and it is the only order-router change in the window, so any key-format or retry-client change would most likely sit there.
No idempotency miss lines appear before 14:10:11Z, so the misses start abruptly.

contradicting.text: The first miss comes about 8 minutes after the deploy, and the duplicate_orders metric was 0 until 14:10. A TTL or store-side change would fit the same timing, so the timing does not point to a key-format change at rollout.
order-router error rate and latency are flat, and no startup or restart lines appear in the window, so nothing marks a rollout event near the onset.
The change record has no diff or library name, so what changed is unknown.

hypotheses.statement: Slow broker-gateway responses made an upstream caller or WhatsApp time out and resend the same message, producing the retried webhooks. This explains the retries but not why the dedupe lookup misses, so it is at most a trigger that pairs with H1 or H2.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: wa-webhook webhook_retries_pct rose from 0 at 14:09 to 0.117 in the 14:10 bucket, plateauing at 0.35 by 14:12, which matches the onset of retries. broker-gateway also logged a slow response at 14:09:01Z.

contradicting.text: No timeout or error lines appear in broker-gateway. wa-webhook logs show no redeliveries or response timeouts, and no repeated message IDs were enqueued.
Slow broker responses are sparse (14:05, 14:09, 14:13, 14:15), and none is tied to the retries.
Even if it caused retries, this does not explain why the dedupe lookup misses, so it is at most a trigger alongside H1 or H2.

hypotheses.statement: Orchestrator re-processes redelivered inbound-msgs messages (at-least-once consumption) and issues a second broker-gateway call, creating duplicate orders independent of order-router dedupe.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: broker-gateway has two synchronous callers, orchestrator and order-router, so a duplicate submission could arrive via either path.
It is possible that an at-least-once redelivery of inbound-msgs makes orchestrator issue a second broker call, but this is unverified.

contradicting.text: RabbitMQ shows zero errors and flat latency, and there is no evidence of a redelivery storm.
orchestrator logs and metrics show no change at 14:10 (latency, rps, errors), and the orchestrator-to-order-router edge is inconsistent in the graph. DEBUG-level activity was not checked.

facts.text: order-router duplicate_orders metric is 0.0 in every 5-minute bucket from 13:10 through 14:05 and first rises at 14:10:00Z to 5.4.
order-router err_rate stays low (max 0.005) and latency_ms mean is 180.044, so the duplicates do not show as a general error spike.

order-router's error rate and latency stayed in a narrow band. The summary shows err_rate max 0.005 and latency_ms max 193.273, with no spike visible, which does not support a timeout-driven failure inside order-router.

broker-gateway logged a slow broker response at 14:09:01Z, about a minute before the first duplicate-treatment warning. Earlier slow responses were logged at 14:05:57Z. No timeout or error lines appeared at WARN and above in this window.

wa-webhook's only WARN lines in the 13:50-14:25Z window were health-probe messages about a missing signature header. None describe WhatsApp redeliveries or response timeouts, which weakens the webhook-redelivery hypothesis but does not rule it out.
RabbitMQ's error rate was zero for the whole window and its latency stayed between 1.865 and 2.11 ms. This does not support a queue-side failure or redelivery storm.
order-router deployed a 'dependency bump' at 14:02 UTC, about 8 minutes before the reported ~14:10 duplicate orders.

redis-cache configuration changed at 14:07 UTC: maxmemory reduced from 4gb to 1gb and eviction policy set to allkeys-lru. This is before the ~14:10 duplicates. If redis holds order dedupe or idempotency keys, eviction could drop them.

order-router's direct synchronous dependencies are broker-gateway (weight 0.8) and postgres (weight 0.3); web-app calls it (weight 0.5). No queue edges were returned for order-router, and redis-cache does not appear among its direct edges.
broker-gateway has two synchronous callers in the graph: orchestrator (0.3) and order-router (0.8). A duplicate submission reaching broker-gateway could come from either path.
orchestrator is listed as a caller of order-router (weight 0.3), but orchestrator's own dependency list does not include an order-router call. This edge is inconsistent across results.
redis-cache evicted_keys is 0.0 in the 14:09 bucket and jumps to 6000.0 in the 14:10 bucket, so evictions start at 14:10, not at 14:07.
evicted_keys reaches 12000.0 by the 14:11 bucket and stays there through 14:29, so it does not keep rising after 14:11.
The first redis-cache eviction log line is at 14:10:35Z, which is after the 14:10:11Z duplicate-path warnings from E-003, so eviction does not precede the first duplicate in these results.
order-router returned no INFO log lines containing 'redis' between 13:50 and 14:30, so the logs do not show which dedupe store order-router uses.
order-router deploy 00601 at 14:02 is recorded only as a 'dependency bump', with no source or url attached, so the changed library and diff are not available from change history.
Querying all four change kinds for order-router from 13:10 to 15:10 returned only the single 14:02 deploy, with no config, migration or flag change for order-router in the window.
wa-webhook webhook_retries_pct is at baseline 0.0 through 14:09 and first rises in the 14:10 bucket to 0.117.
wa-webhook webhook_retries_pct reaches its plateau of 0.35 by 14:12 and stays there through 14:29.

wa-webhook logged 31 INFO 'enqueued to inbound-msgs' lines from 13:50 to 14:30 (total 31, not truncated), and every message ID in them is distinct. The 14:10-14:14 lines also show no repeated IDs, so no re-enqueue of an already-enqueued message is logged.
broker-gateway logged two more slow-broker WARN lines in the window, at 14:13:48Z and 14:15:50Z. These are in addition to the 14:09:01Z line already recorded.
redis-cache's direct callers in the graph are orchestrator (weight 0.3) and portfolio-svc (weight 0.2). order-router is not listed as a caller of redis-cache.
redis-cache memory_pct was 60.02 in the 14:09 bucket, rose to 77.195 in the 14:10 bucket and reached 97.0 in the 14:11 bucket.
The 14:07 redis-cache configuration change shows no step in memory_pct: values stayed near 57-59% from 14:06 to 14:08, and evicted_keys stayed at 0.0 from 14:05 to 14:09.
The order-router idempotency-filtered query for 14:00:00-14:10:15Z returned exactly 3 lines, all misses, with none earlier than 14:10:11Z and no hit lines.
The 'start' search over 14:00:00-14:10:15Z returned no lines, so no startup or restart line is logged in the window.
orchestrator err_rate is flat at 0.004 across 14:09-14:18 and does not change at 14:10:00, so there is no error signal from orchestrator at the incident onset.

The first WARN eviction line in 14:10:00-14:11:00 is at 14:10:35Z. No WARN eviction line appears at 14:10:11Z or earlier in that window, so no eviction is logged there before the 14:10:11Z duplicate-path warning.

A later WARN eviction line at 14:10:57Z uses the same count text, '6000 evicted', as the 14:10:35Z line. The line names no keys or key prefixes, so the evicted key identities are not recoverable from logs.

assumptions.text: The retries may have been triggered by the slow broker-gateway responses at 14:05-14:09Z, which could have pushed a caller past its timeout. The link between the two is not shown in the logs.

Duplicate submission candidates: orchestrator re-processing a redelivered inbound-msgs message (at-least-once consumption) would issue a second broker-gateway call. order-router is a second possible source if it is retried or re-invoked. Both are unverified without retry and idempotency config.

If the duplicate path is caused by a key-format or retry-client change, it most likely sits inside the 14:02 order-router-00601 dependency bump, since no other order-router change appears in the change history for the window. This is not confirmed, because the diff is not available to me.

Evicted keys may include order-dedupe or idempotency keys, which would explain a missing-key warning in order-router. This is not verified: no key names or prefixes were queried, and the caller that reads these keys is not confirmed.

Memory did not reach the configured limit before 14:10:11Z. The 14:09 bucket is at 60.02 and the first eviction log is at 14:10:35Z, but the 14:10 bucket (77.195) spans 14:10:11Z, so the crossing cannot be placed.

The first miss is about 8 minutes after the 14:02 deploy, not immediately after it. That spacing does not by itself show a key-format change at rollout. A TTL or age-based expiry, or a store-side change, would fit the same timing equally well. This is not tested.

Orchestrator is unlikely to be the duplicate source. Its logs show no retry or redelivery activity, and its metrics show no change at 14:10 in latency, throughput or errors. This is inferred from INFO+ logs and does not rule out DEBUG-level activity or a redelivery that is not logged.

order-router's idempotency check more likely reads postgres than redis-cache, because postgres is its only storage-like sync dependency in the graph and redis-cache has no edge from it. The source or config has not been read, so this is unverified.

unresolved: The cause of the missing idempotency keys is not established. It is not known whether order-router stores them in postgres or redis-cache, nor their TTL.

actions.text: Inspect the order-router-00601 diff and runtime configuration to identify which dependency changed and whether idempotency-key generation or the retry client changed. If it is implicated, prepare a rollback to the previous release.
actions.rationale: This is the only order-router change in the window. Its content is unknown, and a rollback is the fastest way to test H2 and stop the duplicates if it is the cause.

actions.text: Determine where order-router stores idempotency keys (postgres or redis-cache) and their TTL, from source or config. Then check whether keys with that prefix still exist and were evicted or expired.
actions.rationale: The store and TTL are unknown, and this decides whether the redis-cache eviction (H1) or something else explains the missing keys.

actions.text: Pull broker-gateway execution or fill records and order IDs for 14:10 onward to confirm whether two broker orders were actually executed per message, and size the customer impact. Reconcile affected customers' positions.
actions.rationale: The warnings do not name order IDs and broker-gateway INFO logs carry no submission data, so actual double execution is not confirmed. The duplicate_orders metric is still at 18.0 at the end of the window.

actions.text: Re-evaluate the redis-cache maxmemory setting. Memory reached 97% and evictions continued after the 14:07 change, so consider restoring capacity if redis holds any dedupe keys.
actions.rationale: Memory pressure and steady evictions persist, and capacity restoration is low-risk. It is justified by the eviction data, though a link to the duplicates is unproven.

actions.text: Check wa-webhook and rabbitmq for retry and redelivery sources: webhook response time to WhatsApp, DEBUG logs, inbound-msgs redelivery and requeue metrics, and consumer restarts.
actions.rationale: The origin of the retried webhooks is unknown, and webhook_retries_pct rose at the same time as the duplicates.

actions.text: Add duplicate-detection logging that includes the message ID, idempotency key and order ID in the order-router warnings, and alert on duplicate_orders above zero.
actions.rationale: The current warnings carry no IDs, so duplicates cannot be joined to orders, and the metric's unit is undocumented.

actions.text: Review change-management for the redis-cache memory reduction, including checking which services depend on keys that live in redis-cache (including the orchestrator, which calls it) before reducing limits.
actions.rationale: A 4gb to 1gb cut was followed by sustained evictions at 97% memory, and the dependents' key usage is unmapped.
